title: Fine-Tuning Small Reasoning Models for Quantum Field Theory
abstract: arXiv:2604.18936v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Despite the growing application of large language models (LLMs) to theoretical physics, there has been little academic exploration of how domain-specific physics reasoning ability develops during training. To investigate this, we perform the first academic comparison of reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning for LLMs on verifiable problem-solving tasks in theoretical physics. Because the open-source verifiable training data required to develop such capabilities is scarce, we built a robust data generation pipeline that can both create synthetic problems and make existing human-authored problems suitable for model training. Selecting quantum field theory (QFT) as our primary domain, we generated over 2,500 synthetic problems alongside a curated collection of human-adapted problems sourced from arXiv and standard pedagogical resources. We conduct both reinforcement learning (RL) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) experiments,

translated_title: 针对量子场论的小型推理模型微调
translated_abstract: 尽管大语言模型（LLM）在理论物理中的应用日益增多，但关于领域特定的物理推理能力在训练过程中如何发展的学术探索仍然很少。为了研究这一问题，我们首次从学术角度对大语言模型在理论物理可验证问题求解任务上的强化学习与监督微调进行了比较。由于开发此类能力所需的开源可验证训练数据十分稀缺，我们构建了一个稳健的数据生成管线，它既能创建合成问题，又能将现有的人类撰写问题改造为适合模型训练的形式。我们选择量子场论（QFT）作为主要领域，生成了超过2,500个合成问题，并整理了一个精选的、来自arXiv和标准教学资源的人类改编问题集合。我们开展了强化学习（RL）和监督微调（SFT）两类实验，
tldr: 本文首次对大语言模型在理论物理可验证任务上的强化学习与监督微调进行学术比较，并构建了可生成超过2,500个量子场论问题的数据管线来微调小型推理模型。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first academic comparison of reinforcement learning versus supervised fine-tuning for LLMs on verifiable theoretical physics tasks, enabled by a robust data generation pipeline that produced over 2,500 quantum field theory problems for training small reasoning models.
